cases.expected: A JsonMetaSchema instance that equals JsonSchemaVersion.DRAFT_07.getInstance() (i.e., the meta‑schema for Draft‑07). No call to loadMetaSchema should occur.
cases.description: The supplied id is a recognised JSON‑Schema dialect. The method should detect the version, map it through checkVersion, obtain the corresponding JsonSchemaVersion instance and return its JsonMetaSchema. This covers the true‑branch of the Optional.map chain.
Another well‑known dialect (2020‑12). Verifies that the method works for any dialect that SpecVersionDetector can resolve, not just Draft‑07.

cases.expected: A JsonMetaSchema instance that equals JsonSchemaVersion.DRAFT_04.getInstance().
cases.description: Ensures older dialects are also correctly resolved via the Optional path.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by JsonSchemaFactory.loadMetaSchema("urn:custom:my-meta-schema", config). The test should verify that loadMetaSchema is invoked exactly once and that its result is returned.
cases.description: The id is not recognised by SpecVersionDetector, so the Optional is empty and the lambda supplied to orElseGet is executed. This covers the fallback branch.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema(null, config). The method should not throw NPE; it should delegate to loadMetaSchema.
cases.description: Edge case where the id argument is null. The detection step should return Optional.empty, causing the fallback to be taken. Verifies robust handling of null ids.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema("", config).
cases.description: Empty string id, also not a known dialect, should trigger the fallback branch.

cases.expected: A JsonMetaSchema instance equal to JsonSchemaVersion.DRAFT_07.getInstance(). The method must handle a null SchemaValidatorsConfig without throwing, and must not invoke loadMetaSchema.
cases.description: Null config with a well‑known dialect should still resolve the dialect via SpecVersionDetector and return the corresponding meta‑schema, proving that the config argument is optional for the true branch.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema("urn:custom:my-meta-schema", null). The fallback branch must be taken and the null config must be forwarded to loadMetaSchema.
cases.description: Null config with an unknown id forces the fallback; verifies that the method forwards a null config unchanged to loadMetaSchema and does not throw NPE.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema("  http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#  ", config). Because the id contains surrounding whitespace, SpecVersionDetector does not recognise it, so the fallback branch is executed.
cases.description: Tests that the detection logic is strict about whitespace; the method should treat the id as unknown and delegate to loadMetaSchema.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema("HTTP://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/DRAFT-07/SCHEMA#", config). Upper‑case scheme/host makes the id unrecognised, causing fallback.
cases.description: Ensures that id matching is case‑sensitive; a well‑known dialect written in upper case should not be detected and must trigger the custom‑schema path.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema("not a uri", config). SpecVersionDetector cannot parse the string, so Optional.empty leads to fallback.
cases.description: Validates that arbitrary non‑URI strings are safely handed over to loadMetaSchema without causing an exception.

cases.expected: The JsonMetaSchema returned by loadMetaSchema("http://[invalid-ip]/schema#", config). Even though the URI is syntactically invalid, the method should not attempt to resolve it as a known dialect and must fall back.
cases.description: Checks robustness when the id is a malformed URI; the method should treat it as unknown and delegate to loadMetaSchema.

group: Repeated calls with same unknown id (caching behavior)

cases.expected: First call: loadMetaSchema is invoked and its result cached. Second call: loadMetaSchema is NOT invoked again; the cached JsonMetaSchema is returned.
cases.description: Ensures that for an unknown id the factory caches the loaded meta‑schema, preventing duplicate loading on subsequent calls.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or a subclass such as URISyntaxException wrapped in IllegalArgumentException) thrown by SpecVersionDetector.detectOptionalVersion because the supplied id is not a syntactically valid URI.
cases.description: The id contains an illegal host component that cannot be parsed as a URI. The detector should fail before the Optional chain is built, causing the method to propagate the exception.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown by SpecVersionDetector.detectOptionalVersion due to presence of a control character in the URI string.
cases.description: A string containing a null character is not a valid URI. The detector is expected to reject it and throw an IllegalArgumentException, which should bubble up from getMetaSchema.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or a custom ResourceNotFoundException) thrown by loadMetaSchema because the class‑path resource cannot be located.
cases.description: The id points to a class‑path location that does not exist. The fallback branch is taken, and loadMetaSchema should raise an exception indicating that the meta‑schema cannot be loaded.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown by loadMetaSchema when it attempts to read a non‑existent file.
cases.description: A file‑URI that points to a missing file forces loadMetaSchema to fail, verifying that the method propagates the appropriate exception rather than silently returning null.

cases.expected: UncheckedIOException (or IOException wrapped in a RuntimeException) thrown by loadMetaSchema when a network‑level I/O problem occurs while fetching the schema.
cases.description: The id resolves to a remote HTTP resource. Simulating a network failure (e.g., by mocking the HTTP client to throw IOException) should cause loadMetaSchema to propagate an unchecked I/O exception.

cases.expected: UncheckedIOException thrown by loadMetaSchema when it cannot open the JAR entry.
cases.description: Accessing a JAR‑URL that points to a non‑existent JAR file triggers an I/O error inside loadMetaSchema, which must be wrapped and re‑thrown as an unchecked exception.
